# Cost model results (round 8, generated by cost_model.py; model v5, 2026-11-15: checker moved out of the baseline; customer increment defined; answer table added)

All usage numbers are unvalidated assumptions; PLACEHOLDER and PROVISIONAL mark inputs without a source. Prices: AWS Frankfurt list prices, 2026-11-11, a comparison basis only. Savings and break-even hold only **under these assumptions**. Round 4's 95/90/80% is the share of problems the catalogue **supports**, not the share resolved automatically.

## Final summary: cost per cluster per month, hosted AI or an in-cluster GPU (base scenario)

Columns: **Orvex operating cost** is cash. **Customer increment** is the *indicative* cloud-priced value of Nightshift's extra CPU, RAM and disk (not a bill; see the answer table). **Model host and GPU** is the AI option's own cost (cash or amortised cash); EKS rental already includes the instance's CPU, RAM and power, so nothing is added twice. **Combined estimate** adds the three and therefore mixes cash with indicative value. Figures assume comparable workloads; model quality and the model's resource use are untested.

| AI option | 100: Orvex | 100: customer increment | 100: model host and GPU | 100: combined | 10,000: Orvex | 10,000: customer increment | 10,000: model host and GPU | 10,000: combined |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted AI | $422 | $64.76 | $0.00 | $487 | $10.81 | $64.76 | $0.00 | $75.57 |
| Existing customer GPU (L4-class, power only) | $422 | $64.76 | $7.88 | $495 (incomplete subtotal) | $10.79 | $64.76 | $7.88 | $83.43 (incomplete subtotal) |
| New 24 GB GPU (Danny's ~$1,000) | $422 | $64.76 | $94.44 | $581 | $10.79 | $64.76 | $94.44 | $170 |
| New 96 GB GPU (Danny's ~$10,000; listings ~$14-16k) | $422 | $64.76 | $557 | $1,044 | $10.79 | $64.76 | $557 | $633 |
| EKS GPU instance, always on (g6.xlarge) | $422 | $64.76 | $735 | $1,222 | $10.79 | $64.76 | $735 | $810 |
| EKS GPU instance, on demand (g6.xlarge) | $422 | $64.76 | $30.27 | $517 | $10.79 | $64.76 | $30.27 | $106 |
| *Without Nightshift (Orvex only)* | $422 | – | – | $422 | $48.75 | – | – | $48.75 |

Notes: the existing-GPU row counts GPU power only (a partial cost: host CPU, RAM and server use are missing), so its combined figure is an incomplete subtotal. New-GPU rows include a host share that is a PLACEHOLDER. The customer increment is the same in every row; the model's own host resources are separate. Biggest drivers: Orvex's people (round-the-clock cover at 100 clusters; the share of problems needing a person at 10,000), Nightshift's in-cluster footprint and whether spare capacity absorbs it, and the GPU choice.

## Answer: cost per cluster per month (base scenario, v5)

All figures are estimates under labelled assumptions; nothing is measured. Orvex figures are cash. Customer figures are resources first, then an *indicative* value at AWS Frankfurt on-demand prices, which is not a bill. Hosted and in-cluster AI are not assumed to give equal quality.

| Case | Orvex cost per cluster | Customer: extra resources | Customer: indicative value of those resources | Customer: AI hardware | Without Nightshift (Orvex cost) | Orvex saving (+) or extra cost (-) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted AI, 100 clusters | $422 | 1.46 vCPU, 2.8 GiB RAM, 2 GB disk | $64.76 | none (Orvex pays tokens: $0.02) | $422 | -$0.62 |
| In-cluster AI, 100 clusters | $422 | 1.46 vCPU, 2.8 GiB RAM, 2 GB disk, plus the model's own GPU and host resources (not sized) | $64.76 | per option below | $422 | -$0.60 |
| Hosted AI, 10,000 clusters | $10.81 | 1.46 vCPU, 2.8 GiB RAM, 2 GB disk | $64.76 | none (Orvex pays tokens: $0.02) | $48.75 | $37.94 |
| In-cluster AI, 10,000 clusters | $10.79 | 1.46 vCPU, 2.8 GiB RAM, 2 GB disk, plus the model's own GPU and host resources (not sized) | $64.76 | per option below | $48.75 | $37.96 |

**In-cluster AI hardware, per cluster that uses it, per month** (only where the customer wants it; most customers are not assumed to buy a GPU):

| Option | Cost per month | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Existing spare 24 GB datacenter GPU (L4-class) | $7.88 | already owned: power only; no purchase |
| Existing spare 24 GB consumer GPU | $38.33 | already owned: power only |
| New 24 GB GPU (Danny's ~$1,000 option) | $94.44 | purchase spread over 36 months + power + host share + maintenance |
| New 96 GB GPU (Danny's ~$10,000 option; listings ~$14-16k) | $557 | purchase spread over 36 months + power + host share + maintenance |
| EKS GPU instance g6.xlarge, always on | $735 | rented, list price |
| EKS GPU instance started on demand | $30.27 | rented by the hour; warm window and start-up delay are PLACEHOLDERS |

Boundary: hardware or instance, power, hosting share and maintenance. Excluded: staff time to run models, evaluation, spares. Wattages, load, PUE, electricity prices, host shares and maintenance rates are PLACEHOLDERS (see the source table).

**Actual extra spending for the customer vs indicative value:**

- **Resources (estimate):** 1.46 vCPU, 2.8 GiB RAM, 2 GB disk per cluster (research §9 envelope midpoints; 10 nodes).
- **Indicative value:** $64.76 a month at Frankfurt on-demand prices. This is what the capacity would cost if bought as cloud capacity, not what the customer pays.
- **If spare capacity exists:** no new server or node is bought. Power, cooling, storage and network for that load are still real costs; they are **not estimated** (missing: measured power per vCPU on customer hardware, and the customer's network prices).
- **If no spare capacity exists:** capacity is added in whole steps, for example 1 m7i.large node ≈ $88.15 a month on EKS list price; bigger clusters or the high scenario can need more than one. On OMK it means buying or reallocating hardware (price unknown).
- **Disk on EKS** (Nightshift's audit and outbox volume) is real spending even with spare compute.

**Orvex saving (base scenario):**

| Scale | Per cluster per month | Fleet per month | Fleet per year | With $50k / $130k engineer-year |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 clusters | -$0.62 | -$62.09 | -$745 | -$0.62 / -$0.62 per cluster |
| 10,000 clusters | $37.94 | $379,387 | $4,552,646 | $18.83 / $49.41 per cluster |

Scenario range at 10,000 clusters (Orvex saving per cluster per month): low $20.45, base $37.94, high $64.76.

## Staffing at 100 clusters (Orvex engineers; hands-on hours a day across the fleet)

FTE = the larger of (a) cover: someone on duty at all hours, and (b) work: incident hands-on hours plus catalogue/release work, done by the same engineers. Waiting time is not workload. Kubernetes/AWS self-healing and grouping are credited equally in both cases. **No time below is measured.**

| Scenario | Orvex hours/day with Nightshift | FTE with Nightshift | Orvex hours/day without | FTE without |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Work-type split, low (supported 95%) | 0.1 | 5.0 | 1.4 | 5.0 |
| Work-type split, base (supported 90%) | 0.4 | 5.0 | 2.7 | 5.0 |
| Work-type split, high (supported 80%) | 1.1 | 5.0 | 5.0 | 5.0 |
| PRD average: 90% automatic, 20 min (single average) | 0.2 | 5.0 | 1.7 | 5.0 |
| PRD stress: 60% automatic, 45 min (single average) | 1.5 | 5.0 | 3.8 | 5.0 |

Base work-type breakdown with Nightshift (Orvex hands-on hours a day): approval-only 0.1, manual repair 0.1, investigation 0.1; customer/provider hands-on 0.6 h a day (not Orvex). Night: 0.2 h of hands-on work → 1.0 person(s) on a 12 h night duty.

Sensitivity is not shown at this scale: round-the-clock cover sets the FTE in every case.

## AI variants: replaces T2 for a cluster that uses it (per cluster per month)

Boundary for every row: hardware or instance, power, hosting share and hardware maintenance. **Excluded everywhere:** staff time to run and update models, evaluation, spares, and the customer's own server. Capability is **not** equivalent: a 24 GB card runs smaller models than hosted Haiku or Sonnet, and quality is untested (PRD: compare local and hosted on the same cases).

Sources: L4 72 W and g6.xlarge $1.0064/h verified; Danny's $1,000 / 24 GB and $10,000 / 96 GB are his hypotheses (a $1,000 24 GB card is not verified); 96 GB cards listed at $14,080-16,000 (brief addendum, Codex). **PLACEHOLDERS:** consumer card 350 W, 96 GB card 600 W, 40% average load, PUE 1.5, electricity $0.15/0.25/0.35 per kWh, host share $20/$40, maintenance 10% a year, the 1 h/day warm window. GPU start-up delay is unverified.

| Variant | low | base | high |
|---|---|---|---|
| existing spare 24 GB datacenter GPU (L4-class, 72 W): power only | $4.73 | $7.88 | $11.04 |
| existing spare 24 GB consumer GPU (~350 W, assumption): power only | $23.00 | $38.33 | $53.66 |
| new 24 GB consumer GPU (~$1,000, Danny): 36-month amortisation + power + host share $20 + maintenance 10%/yr | $79.11 | $94.44 | $110 |
| new 96 GB GPU ($10,000 Danny / $15,000 Codex listing): amortisation + power (~600 W, assumption) + host share $40 + maintenance | $441 | $557 | $674 |
| EKS g6.xlarge (L4) always on | $735 | $735 | $735 |
| EKS g6.xlarge started on demand (0.15 unfamiliar problems/month x 0.5 h, plus 1 h/day warm window) | $0.08 | $30.27 | $60.46 |
| one model server per customer (g6.xlarge always on / 4 clusters per customer) | $184 | $184 | $184 |
| Hosted tokens, Haiku 4.5 regional (round 4) | $0.01 | $0.02 | $0.12 |
| No AI | $0 | $0 | $0 |
